reasons: Worth one run once fixed, as the cleanest test of the new tfx_daily dimension. It is not a duplicate: no earlier test used exchange-published retail positioning, and the direct controls are the right instinct. Data checks (timestamps and states only, no forward returns): the TFX date D lines up with our New York-close D1 bar (TFX settle minus Dukascopy D1 bid close, median 0.02-0.04 yen over 2010-2017 on all five crosses). scripts/build_external_tfx_daily.py documents report header times of 05:10 / 07:10 Tokyo, so ts_avail = D+1 00:00 UTC (09:00 JST) and an entry at 00:15 UTC are credible for today's reports.

BLOCKER, the open-interest state mostly measures the size of the decline. On AUDJPY in design, corr(d_oi_pct, change / ATR20) is -0.62 over all days (NZDJPY -0.55, GBPJPY -0.47, USDJPY -0.50). Among declines of at least 0.25 x ATR20, the mean decline is -0.94 ATR when d_oi_pct >= 6%, -0.74 at 3-6% and -0.59 below 3%. So 'hyp minus no_oi' compares large declines with all declines. The programme has already measured that large one-day moves keep going: fading a >= 1 x ATR20 EURUSD day lost -0.10 R (-0.18 R at 1.25 x) in fx_volume_climax_reversal, and 2-sigma moves kept running in cross_zfade. That follow-the-shock sign must not be registered from those runs. A positive hyp-minus-control gap here could be that size effect dressed up as retail positioning. The state has to be the open-interest change beyond what the day's move already explains.

The oi_down control cannot be read, so the kill rule cannot fire. On AUDJPY in design, a decline of >= 0.25 x ATR20 with d_oi_pct <= -3% occurs 12 times on non-Fridays (6 times at -6%), and 7 (4) times at 0.5 x ATR20. NZDJPY has 15 (9) and USDJPY 7 (5). These are crash days on which open interest fell because positions were cut (mean decline -1.2 to -1.9 ATR). The kill clause is an AND that requires this arm to be at least as good as hyp. With 4-12 trades that comparison is noise, and the family would almost never be closed.

Fixed percentage thresholds are not stationary. Click 365 open interest grew several-fold over the design years, and qualifying AUDJPY events (decline >= 0.25 ATR, d_oi_pct >= 3%) fell from 56-57 a year in 2010-2011 to 18-19 in 2016-2017. The same threshold selects a different share of days every year, and the check period would see yet another share. A trailing, standardised state removes this.

The proxy works on two of the five crosses. Per-year corr(d_oi_pct, change / ATR20) over 2010-2023 is negative in every year for AUDJPY (-0.40 to -0.79) and NZDJPY (-0.24 to -0.78). USDJPY turns positive from 2017 (+0.07 to +0.65 in 2017-2023). EURJPY is +0.03 over the design years and positive in 11 of 14 years. GBPJPY is erratic (+0.02 in 2016, +0.18 in 2017). The weekly long/short split (58 Tuesdays, 2022-11 to 2023-12, before the holdout) shows that the Click 365 book is not structurally long: median long share 0.51 AUDJPY, 0.50 NZDJPY, 0.32 GBPJPY, 0.35 EURJPY, 0.29 USDJPY. Rising open interest on a down day therefore means 'longs added net of shorts covered' where the proxy works, and it means something different on USDJPY, EURJPY and GBPJPY.

The expected counts are overstated. Design AUDJPY events before position blocking, non-Fridays: 235 at (3%, 0.25 ATR), 110 at (6%, 0.25), 178 at (3%, 0.5) and 90 at (6%, 0.5). That is 0.9-2.4 a month, not 3, and every 6% cell is below the pre-registered 120-trade minimum. Friday rows have ts_avail Saturday 00:00 UTC, so the T+15 to T+60 minute entry window holds no bars. 132 of 625 qualifying declines (21%) disappear without being mentioned.

The 'tokyo' hold repeats the cycle-3 window. jpy_cross_losscut_after_us_shock shorted AUDJPY into the Tokyo morning after a weak US session, and the crosses bounced in every arm. The mechanism here (a margin call at the New York close and a forced close at the next business-day deadline) predicts nothing inside the Tokyo session. That arm adds cells without theory, in a window already measured negative. A 0.5 x ATR20 stop on a 24-48 h hold sits inside one day's noise and doubles the cost in R.

This mechanism acts in the tails, so the honest expected effect is small. Japanese retail leverage was capped at 50x in August 2010 and at 25x from August 2011. At typical effective leverage (5-10x), a margin call needs a cumulative adverse move of several ATR; only the most levered accounts are called after a single 0.25-0.5 ATR day. Any edge will come from a few crash episodes (2010-05, 2011-03, 2011-08, 2013-05/06, 2015-08, 2016-01, 2016-06) and may sit in 2010-2011, before the 25x cap. The pre-registered avg R of 0.12 with design t >= 2 is optimistic. About 0.05-0.10 R, with design t about 1-1.5 on 150-300 trades, is realistic.

Speed under the 60-day goal. The stated 0.21 per market and about 0.4 pooled assume weakly correlated crosses, and they are not weakly correlated. TFX daily returns correlate 0.54-0.86 across the five crosses. The 957 events of the five crosses (3%, 0.25 ATR, design, non-Friday) fall on only 552 dates, and 48% of AUDJPY event dates are also NZDJPY event dates. Once the crosses where the proxy fails are dropped, AUDJPY and NZDJPY are close to one stream. At a realistic 0.05-0.10 R and 1.2-3.3 trades a month the score is about 0.06-0.18, and pooled it is about the same. Adding an uncorrelated leg of that size to the parked basket (monthly Sharpe about 0.4) gives about 0.45, against about 2 needed. Even a full pass does not move the 60-day pass rate in a material way. This is an information test of tfx_daily, and a pass would be a recorded slow edge, not a challenge leg.

Costs: medium. At a 1.0 x ATR20 stop, AUDJPY trading costs (about 2 pips round trip: spread, $7 commission, 0.2 pip slippage) are 0.016-0.03 R. A short AUDJPY also pays the AUD-JPY rate differential plus the 1% markup, about 0.008-0.012 R per night-weight in 2010-2014. A 48 h hold therefore costs about 0.05 R all-in, half of the stated edge. At 0.5 x ATR20 the cost is about 0.1 R.

Plumbing. The pipeline's GA floor takes the best of ALL stage A cells by design t, controls included, and report.json keeps only the top 15 rows; the cycle 7 and 8 stage A grids had 24 and 16 cells. The Director must read every stage A cell from runs/research.sqlite and apply the floor and the kill rules to hyp cells only. runs/ also holds a draft of the same family (jpy_retail_dipbuy_fragility: a five-day decline with raw open-interest growth of 10-15%). It is closer to the margin arithmetic but has the same size confound. Run one version only; a second version counts in the same family.
reviews.revisions:
1) State = abnormal open-interest build-up, matched on decline size. For each tfx_daily row i of this pair (rows ordered by ts_avail), fit OLS d_oi_pct ~ a + b x ret on the previous oi_window = 250 rows of the same pair (rows i-250..i-1, at least oi_min_obs = 200 finite pairs; rows before start feed the window). Set z_i = (d_oi_pct_i - a - b x ret_i) / sd, where sd is that window's residual standard deviation (ddof 2). Never fit or standardise on the full sample. Decline as written: change_i <= -decline_atr_min x ATR20. Arms: 'hyp' = decline and z_i >= z_build; 'low' = decline and z_i <= -z_build; 'all' = decline only. Every arm requires a finite z_i. This balances decline size by construction. AUDJPY design at 0.25 ATR split at 0: hyp 314 vs low 311 events, mean decline -0.69 vs -0.74 ATR. At 0.5 ATR with z +/-0.5: 120 vs 107 events, -0.95 vs -1.10 ATR. These replace oi_up_min_pct and arm 'oi_down'.
2) Markets: AUDJPY (primary) and NZDJPY only. Drop USDJPY, EURJPY and GBPJPY, where the proxy's sign flips or is absent.
3) Entry: every qualifying row enters on the next weekday after date D: Monday-Thursday rows on D+1, Friday rows on Monday. Enter at the first bar at or after 00:15 UTC that day, if that bar is no later than 01:00 UTC. The signal bar is the bar before it, and its close time must be at or after T. This recovers the 21% Friday rows.
4) Holds: drop 'tokyo'. Use hold_h in [24, 48]: exit at the open of the first bar at or after 00:00 UTC on the first (24) or second (48) weekday after the entry day. A 24 h trade then closes before the next day's 00:15 entry, so back-to-back days are not blocked. State that signals arriving during an open 48 h trade are skipped (one position at a time).
5) Stop: sl_atr fixed at 1.0, not in the grid.
6) Grids. Spec grid (hyp only): z_build [0.0, 0.5] x decline_atr_min [0.25, 0.5] x hold_h [24, 48] = 8 cells. Stage A grid: arm [hyp, low, all] x the same = 24 cells, 20 distinct because the 'all' cells repeat over z_build. Write stage_a.grid and grid separately in specs/auto/jpy_retail_dip_buying_cascade.json, as in cycles 7 and 8, and update params to the new keys.
7) Kill rules (AUDJPY, design, stage A, every cell read from research.sqlite). K1: among hyp cells with >= 90 design trades, the best by design t must have avg R > 0 and t >= 1; apply this floor to hyp cells only. K2: the mean of (hyp - low) over the 8 settings must be > 0, and (hyp - low) at the best hyp cell's settings must be >= +0.05 R; otherwise kill, because open interest carries no information beyond the decline. K3: the best hyp cell must stay > 0 after removing its three best calendar weeks; otherwise kill, because the edge is a few crash episodes. K4: report 2010-2011 and 2012-2017 separately; if 2012-2017 avg R <= 0 in the best hyp cell, kill, because the edge belongs to the leverage regime before the 25x cap. 'low' and 'all' are never promoted. A low > hyp result, or a positive 'all', must never be registered later as a long-after-build-up or follow-the-decline hypothesis (a snooped flip).
8) Restate pre_registered: expected avg R 0.08; trades per month 1.2-3.3 on AUDJPY depending on the cell (120-314 design events before blocking); expected design t about 1-1.5; minimum 90 design trades; speed about 0.08 x sqrt(2.5) = 0.13 per market. AUDJPY and NZDJPY are close to one stream, so the pooled score is about the same. Say plainly that this cannot reach 0.7, that it tests whether tfx_daily carries information, and that a pass is recorded as a slow edge.
9) Holdout policy under the 60-day goal. Spend the counted holdout run only if the basket step shows that adding this leg to the parked legs raises pass-within-60-days on the 2018+ starts by at least 5 points, with fail-within-60-days not higher. Otherwise record the leg in runs/basket without a holdout touch.
10) Stage C robustness (reported, not gating): rerun the chosen cell with entry at 06:15 UTC on the same entry day. The 09:00 JST availability rests on today's report header times, and the 2010-2017 publication times are undocumented. If the edge exists only with the 00:15 UTC entry, flag it.
reviews.notes_for_builder: Selecting the pair: e = F.ext_series(m, 'tfx_daily'); sel = np.array([s == m.sym for s in e.column('symbol')]) (the column holds None for unmapped pairs); t = F.ext_subset(m, 'tfx_daily', sel). Arrays: T = t.ts_avail; D = t.column('date').astype('datetime64[D]'); chg = t.column('change'); ret = t.column('ret'); oi = t.column('d_oi_pct'). d_oi_pct is a FRACTION (0.03 = 3%). z: loop over rows i. The series is attached from 2005, so the 250-row window exists from the first design day. Use rows i - p['oi_window'] .. i-1 only and require at least p['oi_min_obs'] finite (ret, oi) pairs; b, a = np.polyfit(ret_w, oi_w, 1); sd = std(residuals, ddof=2); z_i = (oi[i] - a - b * ret[i]) / sd; z_i = NaN otherwise. No full-sample statistics anywhere. ATR: daily = F.daily_bars(m); atr = daily.to_bars(F.atr_prev(daily, p['atr_n'])). Read atr at the entry bar ei: its trading day is the entry day, so the ATR covers the 20 days up to and including D. Decline: chg[i] <= -p['decline_atr_min'] * atr[ei] * (1 - 1e-9). Entry day: D + 1 day for Monday-Thursday dates, D + 3 days for Friday (F.weekday(D) == 4); ei = F.first_bar_at_or_after(m, entry_days, 0, 15). Require ei >= 1, ei < m.n, m.ts[ei] <= entry_day + 01:00 UTC, and m.close_times()[ei - 1] >= T[i]. Then sig = ei - 1; entry_short[sig] = True; entry_type 0; valid_bars 1; sl_dist[sig] = p['sl_atr'] * atr[ei] (skip if not finite or <= 0); tp_dist NaN. Exit: x_day = np.busday_offset(entry_day, 1 if hold_h == 24 else 2, roll='forward'); xi = F.first_bar_at_or_after(m, [x_day], 0, 0); if ei < xi < m.n, set exit_short[xi - 1] = True. Do not use a fixed max_bars count, because bars are sparse. arm must be one of 'hyp', 'low', 'all' and z_build must be >= 0; raise ValueError otherwise. Rows with T < start are not traded but still feed the z windows. PARAMS = {'z_build': 0.0, 'decline_atr_min': 0.25, 'hold_h': 24, 'sl_atr': 1.0, 'arm': 'hyp', 'oi_window': 250, 'oi_min_obs': 200, 'entry_utc': '00:15', 'max_entry_delay_min': 45, 'atr_n': 20, 'start': '2010-01-01'}. Module GRID = arm [hyp, low, all] x z_build [0.0, 0.5] x decline_atr_min [0.25, 0.5] x hold_h [24, 48], so the checker exercises every key. Checker expectations (AUDJPY, design 2010-2017, events before position blocking): hyp 314 / 169 / 192 / 120 and low 311 / 157 / 189 / 107 at (0.25, z 0) / (0.25, z 0.5) / (0.5, z 0) / (0.5, z 0.5); NZDJPY hyp 310 / low 303 at (0.25, z 0). The mean decline (change / ATR) of the hyp and low entries should agree within about 0.15 ATR. If hyp's decline is much larger, the residual is wrong (a full-sample fit, or ret and d_oi_pct swapped). Expect a few percent fewer trades after blocking at 24 h and about 15-25% fewer at 48 h. Compare quantised quantities with a 1e-9 relative tolerance.

reasons: Worth one test, but only pooled across the seven pairs; as written it cannot be judged. It is not a duplicate. prior_cot_positioning (P1-P8) used Legacy non-commercial extremes alone with 1-4 week holds and no news trigger, and the post-release tests (NFP follow/fade, the two-hour surprise template, the news-inclusive fade arm) used no positioning state. Crowded leveraged-fund positioning as the state and an adverse surprise as the trigger is a coherent mechanism: crowded speculative currency positions carry crash risk that a shock releases. The neutral control is the right instinct.

BLOCKER, the primary market cannot carry the test. Design events on EURUSD before position blocking: high-impact USD or EUR releases with scraped times, |surprise_z| >= z_min, a 30-minute reaction >= 0.1 x ATR20, and the leveraged-fund percentile over the last 156 reports (at least 52). That gives 46 / 20 / 34 / 16 hyp events in 2011-2017 at (pct 85, z 1.0) / (85, 1.5) / (90, 1.0) / (90, 1.5), about 0.55 a month at best, not 1. Every cell is below the pre-registered 60-trade minimum, so kill rule 3 fires by construction whatever the effect, and half the cells are also below the pipeline's 30-trade floor for choosing the best cell. At 35-45 trades the standard error is about 0.16 R for avg R and about 0.18 R for hyp minus neutral, so the 0.10 R threshold is noise. In the check period EURUSD has 22 / 10 / 16 / 7 events.

The pooled sample has real power. Over the seven pairs at (85, 1.0) there are 421 design hyp events on 294 distinct release times (277 dates): 209 release times trigger one pair and 85 trigger two to five. That is about 3.3 roughly independent event dates a month, plus 175 check events. With release-clustered statistics the standard error is about 0.06-0.07 R, enough to separate 0.15 R from zero. So the family can be judged only as a pooled seven-pair test. The pipeline's stage A is single-market, and scripts/run_backtest.py does not attach external series, so this needs a pooled stage A step.

The controls are incomplete. The neutral arm handles 'post-release drift without crowding'. It does not handle 'reactions keep going in crowded regimes whatever their direction': extreme leveraged-fund positioning comes with strong trends and higher volatility, so a hyp > neutral gap could be regime continuation rather than an unwind. A crowded_with arm (crowded, reaction in the crowd's favour, follow the reaction) separates the two, and it has comparable counts (EURUSD 60 at 85 / 1.0). The background also runs against the hyp side on the primary: fading EUR crowd extremes on EURUSD lost -0.21 to -0.36 R in design in every crowding variant of prior_cot_positioning (P1-P4, 4-week holds).

rank_window 156 with 'first signals in 2011 once 52 reports exist' needs an explicit minimum-reports parameter (an expanding window from 52 to 156 reports). Without it, the Builder either waits for 156 reports and loses 2011-2012 (102 of the 475 EURUSD design triggers), or ranks against a handful of reports.

Trigger hygiene. All design triggers at |z| >= 1 have scraped times, so 'typical' times are not a problem. 'Crude Oil Inventories' supplies 34 of the USD triggers (5.9%). It is an oil-market release and cannot plausibly force leveraged funds out of EUR, GBP, JPY, CHF, AUD or NZD positions, so exclude it on theory (about 6% of the sample). The reference bar 'strictly before R' throws away the M15 bar that closes exactly at R, which holds only pre-release ticks. 'Close time at or before R' is still leak-free and measures the reaction from the true pre-release price.

The holdout is truncated and live use needs a feed. The calendar ends 2025-04-07, so the counted holdout covers 15 of about 33 months (about 40-50 pooled trades). The ForexFactory-derived consensus is for private research only, so a live version needs another source of consensus and actual values. The check period is uneven: 25 of the 43 EUR |z| >= 1.5 rows in 2018-2023 fall in 2020, and USD has 46 such rows in 2020. Check results need to be read with and without 2020.

Speed under the 60-day goal. The stated 0.3 x sqrt(1) = 0.3 per market overstates the frequency: EURUSD has 0.55 events a month in design and about 0.3 in check. At the stated 0.3 R the pooled score is about 0.3 x sqrt(3.3) = 0.55. At a realistic 0.10-0.15 R it is about 0.18-0.27; 0.3 R would be twice the best edge this programme has measured (the gotobi short, about +0.14 R). Neither figure reaches 0.7. Added to the parked basket, it would lift monthly Sharpe from about 0.4 to about 0.5-0.55 at a realistic R, or about 0.9 at the stated R. Of the two hypotheses this cycle, this one has the larger speed ceiling, but it is still a slow-to-moderate leg, not a 60-day solution on its own.

Costs: low. EURUSD costs about 1.3-1.5 pips round trip including commission and slippage, against a 75-pip ATR20, which is about 0.02 R at a 1.0 x ATR20 stop. Entries come 30-45 minutes after the release, when spreads have normalised, and swap over one to three nights is small. The other six pairs cost at most about 0.04 R.
reviews.revisions:
1) Make stage A pooled over the seven pairs; this is required. Run the stage A grid on every pair in the design years, with cot and calendar attached through the pipeline's get_market(..., ext=...) and grid_search (scripts/run_backtest.py does not attach them). Apply the kill rules to the pooled trades, with t clustered by release timestamp. If a pooled stage A cannot be run this cycle, do not run this hypothesis: a single-pair stage A on EURUSD would scrap it on sample size alone. Once the pooled stage A passes, the pipeline's single-market GA floor must not decide the outcome. Either run the pipeline with the floor disabled and say so in the spec notes, or set stage_a.market to the pair with the most hyp events (USDCAD 74, AUDUSD 71 at 85 / 1.0).
2) Grid. Spec grid (hyp only): pct_extreme [85, 90] x hold_h [24, 48], with z_min 1.0 and sl_atr 1.0 fixed = 4 cells. z_min 1.5 halves the sample (EURUSD 20 and 16 events) and the cut has no theory behind it. Stage A grid per pair: arm [hyp, neutral, crowded_with] x the same = 12 cells, 10 distinct because the neutral cells repeat over pct_extreme. That is about 84 counted stage A runs plus 28 in stage B, fewer than the 16 + 16 + 112 of the plan as written.
3) Add arm 'crowded_with': crowded (pct >= pct_extreme or pct <= 100 - pct_extreme) with the reaction moving X in the crowd's favour; trade in the direction of the reaction.
4) Add param min_reports = 52. The percentile ranks the current report among the last min(rank_window, available) reports once at least min_reports exist; before that it is NaN.
5) Exclude event == 'Crude Oil Inventories' from the triggers. Reference price: ref = bid close of the last bar whose close time is at or before R.
6) Exit: count hold_h in weekdays. Exit at the open of the first bar at or after the entry bar's open time moved forward by 1 (24 h) or 2 (48 h) business days at the same UTC clock time. A Friday NFP trade then exits on Monday or Tuesday, not at the Sunday reopen.
7) Kill rules (pooled, design, release-clustered t). K1: the best hyp cell has pooled avg R <= 0.05 or t < 1. K2: pooled hyp minus neutral at the same hold is below +0.10 R. K3: pooled hyp minus crowded_with at the same pct_extreme and hold is <= 0. K4: the best hyp cell has fewer than 150 pooled design trades. Check (pooled): at least 100 trades and avg R > 0, reported with and without 2020. neutral and crowded_with are never promoted, and their signs are never flipped into new hypotheses.
8) Restate pre_registered: expected avg R 0.15 (0.3 would be twice the best edge measured here); trades per month 0.5 per pair in design and 0.3 in check, about 3.3 event dates a month pooled; speed 0.15 x sqrt(3.3) = 0.27 pooled; expected pooled design t about 2. State that the leg cannot reach 0.7 alone.
9) Holdout. State in the spec that the counted holdout covers only 2024-01 to 2025-04-07, where the calendar ends (about 40-50 pooled trades). Spend it only if the basket step shows that the leg raises pass-within-60-days on the 2018+ starts by at least 5 points, with fail-within-60-days not higher. Note that a live version needs a licensed consensus feed.
reviews.notes_for_builder: Currency X and sign: EURUSD, GBPUSD, AUDUSD, NZDUSD have X = base and sgn = +1 (X strengthens when the pair rises); USDJPY, USDCAD, USDCHF have X = quote and sgn = -1. COT: cot = F.ext_series(m, 'cot'); sub = F.ext_subset(m, 'cot', np.array([s == X for s in cot.column('market')])); v = sub.column('spec_net_oi'). For report j: if j + 1 >= p['min_reports'], pct[j] = 100 * mean(v[max(0, j - p['rank_window'] + 1): j + 1] <= v[j]); otherwise NaN. This is row-wise and causal; never rank on the full sample. Map the percentile to bars with idx = np.searchsorted(sub.ts_avail, m.close_times(), side='right') - 1, the same rule F.ext_asof uses; idx < 0 means NaN. Calendar: cal = F.ext_series(m, 'calendar'); trigger mask = (impact == 'high') & time_known & currency in {'USD', X} & finite surprise_z & (abs(surprise_z) >= p['z_min']) & (event != 'Crude Oil Inventories'). Keep one trigger per ts_release; the largest |z| is used only for the threshold. R = ts_release (= ts_avail). Bars: ct = m.close_times(); i_ref = np.searchsorted(ct, R, side='right') - 1 (close at or before R); i_rx = np.searchsorted(ct, R + react_min minutes, side='left'). Skip if i_ref < 0, if i_rx >= m.n - 1, or if ct[i_rx] > R + react_min + 15 minutes (sparse bars). reaction = bid_c[i_rx] - bid_c[i_ref]. Require abs(reaction) >= p['react_atr_min'] * atr[i_rx], with atr = daily.to_bars(F.atr_prev(F.daily_bars(m), p['atr_n'])) finite and > 0. xs = sign(reaction) * sgn (+1 = X strengthened); pc = pct at bar i_rx (skip if NaN). Arms (pe = pct_extreme): hyp = (pc >= pe and xs < 0) or (pc <= 100 - pe and xs > 0); crowded_with = (pc >= pe and xs > 0) or (pc <= 100 - pe and xs < 0); neutral = p['neutral_lo'] <= pc <= p['neutral_hi']; raise ValueError for any other arm. In every arm the side is sign(reaction): long the pair if it rose, short if it fell. Signal on bar i_rx (entry_type 0, valid_bars 1); sl_dist = p['sl_atr'] * atr[i_rx]; tp_dist NaN. Exit: e_open = m.ts[i_rx + 1]; t_x = np.busday_offset(e_open.astype('datetime64[D]'), hold_h // 24, roll='forward') + (e_open - e_open.astype('datetime64[D]')); xi = first bar with ts >= t_x; if xi < m.n, set the exit marker for the trade side on bar xi - 1. Mark every qualifying trigger; the executor skips triggers that arrive while a position is open. PARAMS = {'pct_extreme': 85, 'z_min': 1.0, 'hold_h': 24, 'sl_atr': 1.0, 'arm': 'hyp', 'react_min': 30, 'react_atr_min': 0.1, 'rank_window': 156, 'min_reports': 52, 'neutral_lo': 30, 'neutral_hi': 70, 'atr_n': 20, 'start': '2010-01-01'}. Module GRID = arm [hyp, neutral, crowded_with] x pct_extreme [85, 90] x hold_h [24, 48]. Checker expectations (EURUSD design 2011-2017, events before position blocking, counted with crude inventories included, so expect about 6% fewer): hyp 46, neutral 131, crowded_with 60 at (85, z 1.0); hyp 34 at (90, z 1.0). The first percentile values appear in early 2011. A far lower hyp count usually means the X-strength sign is inverted for the USD/X pairs or the percentile window waits for 156 reports. Compare quantised quantities with a 1e-9 relative tolerance.
